questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from United States of America?

options.text: Centrifugal form of federalism where the centre is stronger than the states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the **Bill of Rights** in the US Constitution. The Indian Constitution guarantees these rights under **Part III**, ensuring basic freedoms and equality to all citizens.
 
• The **American Bill of Rights**, added as the first ten amendments to the US Constitution in 1791, serves as a source of inspiration for ensuring civil liberties such as freedom of speech, religion, and equality before law.
 
• Indian Fundamental Rights include rights like the **Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)**, **Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22)**, and **Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32)**, among others.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, emphasized the importance of Fundamental Rights in ensuring the protection of individual freedoms and societal equality.
 
• Although inspired by the US Constitution, the Indian Fundamental Rights are adapted to align with the socio-political conditions of India, allowing for reasonable restrictions and aligning with the principle of parliamentary sovereignty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centrifugal form of federalism:**

 
 
• The concept of a strong central government in India is not borrowed from the US; instead, it is influenced by the **Government of India Act, 1935**. This system centralizes power, contrary to the US model of federalism, which emphasizes state sovereignty.
 
• Indian federalism is described as **quasi-federal**, with a strong unitary bias, especially during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The concept of the Concurrent List is borrowed from the **Australian Constitution**, not the US. This list allows both the Centre and states to legislate on subjects of common interest.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include education, marriage, and bankruptcy.
 
 
 
• **Single Citizenship:**
 
 
• The concept of single citizenship in India is derived from the **British Constitution**, ensuring that all Indians are citizens of India, irrespective of their state of residence.
 
• This contrasts with the US, where individuals have dual citizenship—one for their state and one for the federal nation.
 
 
 
• **Additional Features Borrowed from the US Constitution:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution also draws inspiration from the US Constitution for features like **judicial review**, the **independence of the judiciary**, and the **impeachment process of the President**.
 
• Other influences include the concept of a **written Constitution** and the division of powers among the **legislature, executive, and judiciary**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights in India are enforceable by courts. Citizens can approach the **Supreme Court under Article 32** or High Courts under **Article 226** for their enforcement.
 
• These rights aim to abolish discrimination, ensure equality, and protect individual liberty.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations to Indian Context:**
 
 
• Unlike the US Bill of Rights, Indian Fundamental Rights include the concept of **reasonable restrictions** to balance individual liberty with societal interests.
 
• For example, **freedom of speech (Article 19)** in India is subject to restrictions based on sovereignty, public order, and morality.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To respect ideals of the constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Separation of judiciary from executive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Part IV-A** of the Indian Constitution under **Article 51A**.
 
• They were added by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** upon the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** include duties such as respecting the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem.
 
• They aim to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• The **separation of judiciary from executive** is not a Fundamental Duty but a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) under **Article 50** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law.
 
• There are a total of **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51A.
 
• Some of the important duties include:
 
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
 
• To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs):**
 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They provide guidelines to the government for establishing social and economic democracy.
 
• The **separation of judiciary from executive** under Article 50 ensures the independence of the judiciary for the proper functioning of the legal system.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Fundamental Duties and DPSPs:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties apply to **citizens**, whereas DPSPs are **guidelines for the state**.
 
• Duties are non-justiciable and aim at inspiring citizens, whereas DPSPs aim to establish socio-economic justice.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**
 
 
• Known as the “**Mini Constitution**” due to the extensive changes made.
 
• Added **Fundamental Duties** and introduced the words “**Socialist**” and “**Secular**” in the Preamble.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• They serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• They are inspired by the **Constitution of the USSR**.
 
• They complement Fundamental Rights by emphasizing responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Article 50:**
 
 
• Part of the DPSPs, it ensures the **independence of the judiciary**.
 
• It mandates that the state shall separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.

questions.question: The 16th Islamic Summit of the OIC will be held in _______ in 2026.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Azerbaijan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **16th Islamic Summit** of the **Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)** is scheduled to be held in **2026**.
 
• The event will take place in **Azerbaijan**, a country known for its active role in the OIC and its efforts to promote unity among Muslim nations.
 
• The **OIC** is the second-largest intergovernmental organization after the United Nations, with a membership of **57 countries**, primarily from the Islamic world.
 
• This summit provides a platform for **collaboration** and addressing **political, economic, cultural, and social issues** affecting member states.
 
• The **previous summit**, the 15th Islamic Summit, was held in **Saudi Arabia**, emphasizing the importance of this periodic gathering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC):**

 
 
• The OIC was established in **1969** following the burning of Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, with the aim of safeguarding the interests of the Muslim world.
 
• It has its headquarters in **Jeddah, Saudi Arabia**.
 
• The OIC works on promoting **international peace and harmony** and addressing issues such as the **Palestinian cause**, Islamophobia, and humanitarian crises.
 
 
 
• **Azerbaijan:**
 
 
• Azerbaijan is a transcontinental country located at the crossroads of **Eastern Europe** and **Western Asia**.
 
• It is a predominantly Muslim country with a rich cultural and historical heritage influenced by both its Islamic and post-Soviet history.
 
• The country has been an **active member** of the OIC since **1991**, shortly after gaining independence from the Soviet Union.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Summits:**
 
 
• The Islamic Summit is the **highest decision-making body** of the OIC, bringing together heads of state to discuss pressing issues.
 
• Past summits have addressed topics such as **Islamophobia, regional conflicts**, and **the advancement of science and technology** in OIC member states.
 
 
 
• **Other Host Countries:**
 
 
• **Gambia:** Though a member of the OIC, it is a smaller nation and has not been chosen as the host for the 16th summit.
 
• **Indonesia:** It is the largest Muslim-majority country by population and has played significant roles in the OIC but is not hosting the 2026 summit.
 
• **Morocco:** Known for its contributions to the Islamic world, it has hosted previous summits but is not the host for the upcoming one.

questions.question: Who among the following was named the goodwill ambassador for Earth Hour India 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P V Sindhu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **P V Sindhu**, a celebrated Indian badminton player, was named the **Goodwill Ambassador for Earth Hour India 2024**.
 
• Earth Hour is a global environmental initiative organized by the **World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF)**. It encourages individuals, communities, and businesses to turn off non-essential electric lights for one hour as a symbol of commitment to the planet.
 
• As the goodwill ambassador, P V Sindhu will raise awareness about the importance of **energy conservation**, combating **climate change**, and adopting sustainable practices.
 
• P V Sindhu's involvement reflects her strong commitment to **environmental conservation** and serves as an inspiration for millions of her fans to participate in this initiative.
 
• The Earth Hour campaign for 2024 aims to focus on **renewable energy** and reducing the carbon footprint, aligning with global efforts to combat climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **P V Sindhu:**

 
 
• P V Sindhu is an **Indian professional badminton player**, born on **5 July 1995** in Hyderabad, India.
 
• She is a recipient of prestigious awards such as the **Padma Bhushan**, **Padma Shri**, and **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award**.
 
• Her landmark achievements include winning a **silver medal** at the **2016 Rio Olympics** and a **bronze medal** at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
• She is known for her **dedication**, **discipline**, and the ability to inspire young athletes across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Earth Hour:**
 
 
• Earth Hour was first launched in **2007** by the **WWF** in Sydney, Australia, and has since grown into a global movement.
 
• It is observed annually on the **last Saturday of March**, when participants turn off lights for one hour, from 8:30 PM to 9:30 PM local time.
 
• The movement aims to spread awareness about **environmental challenges** such as **climate change**, **deforestation**, and **energy conservation**.
 
• Earth Hour 2024 will focus on promoting the adoption of **renewable energy** and reducing **greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
 
 
• **World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF):**
 
 
• WWF, founded in **1961**, is one of the world’s leading organizations dedicated to **conserving nature** and reducing the most pressing threats to biodiversity.
 
• The organization operates in over **100 countries** and has over **5 million supporters** worldwide.
 
• Key WWF initiatives include protecting endangered species, conserving forests, reducing plastic pollution, and addressing climate change.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Goodwill Ambassadors:**
 
 
• In past years, several influential personalities such as **actors, athletes, and environmentalists** have served as Earth Hour ambassadors.
 
• These ambassadors play a crucial role in engaging the public and spreading the message of sustainability and conservation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India and Earth Hour:**

 
 
• India has been a strong participant in the Earth Hour movement, with several landmarks such as the **India Gate** and **Gateway of India** going dark to support the cause.
 
• Various schools, colleges, and organizations actively participate to raise awareness about **energy conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change and Energy Conservation:**
 
 
• Climate change is one of the most significant challenges of the 21st century, with rising global temperatures and extreme weather events posing threats to ecosystems and communities.
 
• Energy conservation and the adoption of renewable energy sources are critical steps to **mitigate climate change**.

questions.question: Har Gobind Khorana won the Nobel Prize in which field in 1968?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medicine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Har Gobind Khorana** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Medicine** in the year **1968**. He shared this prestigious award with **Robert W. Holley** and **Marshall W. Nirenberg**.
 
• The Nobel Prize was awarded to them for their **interpretation of the genetic code** and its function in **protein synthesis**. This groundbreaking work provided profound insights into how DNA operates within living organisms.
 
• Har Gobind Khorana and his colleagues demonstrated how **nucleotides** in DNA determine the **amino acid sequence** of proteins, elucidating the essential principles of **genetics and molecular biology**.
 
• This research was instrumental in advancing the field of **genetic engineering** and paved the way for further studies on DNA sequencing and biotechnology.
 
• Their work also contributed to the understanding of the **triplet nature of the genetic code**, showing that three nucleotides (codons) specify one amino acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Har Gobind Khorana’s Background:**

 
 
• Har Gobind Khorana was born on **January 9, 1922**, in **Raipur, Punjab (now in Pakistan)**.
 
• He pursued his higher education in **biochemistry** and specialized in the field of **genetics and molecular biology**.
 
• Khorana became a naturalized citizen of the **United States** and conducted much of his Nobel-winning research there.
 
 
 
• **Nobel Prize-Winning Research:**
 
 
• The **genetic code** research demonstrated that the sequence of nucleotides in DNA determines the sequence of amino acids in proteins.
 
• The discovery of the **triplet code** (codons) revealed the mechanism by which DNA instructions are translated into functional proteins.
 
• Their work also defined the **start and stop codons**, which play a crucial role in the initiation and termination of protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Applications of His Work:**
 
 
• Khorana's research laid the foundation for **genetic engineering**, which has applications in medicine, agriculture, and biotechnology.
 
• It has been pivotal in the development of **DNA-based diagnostics** and therapies for genetic disorders.
 
• The understanding of protein synthesis has also contributed to advancements in **drug development** and treatment strategies for diseases like cancer.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions:**
 
 
• Khorana was one of the first scientists to synthesize **oligonucleotides**, which are short DNA or RNA molecules. This technology is now widely used in genetic research and medicine.
 
• His work also contributed to the development of techniques for **gene sequencing and editing**.
 
• Khorana’s contributions are celebrated globally, and he remains a key figure in the history of molecular biology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nobel Prize in Medicine (Physiology or Medicine):**

 
 
• This is one of the six Nobel Prizes established by the will of **Alfred Nobel** in 1895.
 
• It is awarded annually for outstanding contributions to the field of **medical science**.
 
• Notable recipients include **Alexander Fleming** for the discovery of penicillin and **Watson, Crick, and Wilkins** for the discovery of the structure of DNA.
 
 
 
• **Triplet Genetic Code:**
 
 
• The genetic code is composed of sequences of three nucleotides, also known as **codons**.
 
• Each codon corresponds to a specific **amino acid**, which is a building block of proteins.
 
• The discovery of the triplet code was crucial in understanding how genes direct the synthesis of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Genetic Engineering:**
 
 
• Genetic engineering has revolutionized fields such as **agriculture** (e.g., genetically modified crops) and **medicine** (e.g., gene therapy).
 
• It has also enabled the production of **recombinant proteins**, such as insulin and vaccines.

questions.question: In November 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was honoured with the Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award for Minority Upliftment in which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** was awarded the **Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award** in November 2024 for his contributions towards **minority upliftment** and promotion of peace globally.
 
• The **Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award** is a prestigious honor conferred in the **United States of America**, recognizing leaders who contribute to societal harmony and advocate for the rights of minorities.
 
• The award acknowledges Modi's efforts in empowering minorities in India through initiatives like **educational reforms, economic upliftment programs, and inclusive policies**.
 
• The United States holds a significant position in acknowledging global leaders for their contributions to peace, equality, and human rights, aligning with **Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s legacy**.
 
• This recognition further strengthens the diplomatic relationship between **India and the United States**, emphasizing the global impact of Modi's leadership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.**:

 
 
• He was a prominent leader of the **American civil rights movement** and is renowned for advocating **non-violent resistance**.
 
• His famous speech, "**I Have a Dream**," delivered in 1963, is a pivotal moment in American history, emphasizing **racial equality and justice**.
 
• The **Martin Luther King Jr. Day**, observed annually in January in the United States, commemorates his legacy and contributions.
 
 
 
• **Minority Upliftment in India:**
 
 
• Under Modi's leadership, initiatives like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)** aim to improve infrastructure in minority-concentrated areas.
 
• Programs like "**Seekho aur Kamao**" focus on skill development for minority youths.
 
• The introduction of scholarships such as the **Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships** for minorities has significantly enhanced educational opportunities.
 
• Emphasis on **entrepreneurship development** through schemes like "**Stand-Up India**" ensures economic empowerment.
 
 
 
• **India-U.S. Relations:**
 
 
• The relationship between India and the United States has strengthened under Modi's leadership through **bilateral trade, defense collaborations, and cultural exchanges**.
 
• Initiatives like **India-U.S. Strategic Partnership Forum** highlight the shared interests in global peace and development.
 
• Recognition of Indian leaders like Modi in the U.S. underscores the importance of India's global leadership role.
 
 
 
• **Global Peace Awards:**
 
 
• These awards serve to honor individuals who work towards **peacebuilding, human rights, and societal development**.
 
• Such recognition promotes the values of global harmony and reinforces the efforts of leaders in addressing **critical issues like inequality, discrimination, and poverty**.
 
• Past recipients include figures like **Barack Obama** and **Malala Yousafzai**, who have contributed significantly to global peace and justice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Global Peace Award:**

 
 
• Recognizes contributions to **peacebuilding and minority upliftment**.
 
• Named after the iconic leader who advocated for **non-violent resistance and racial equality**.
 
• Signifies international acknowledgment of leaders promoting **human rights and inclusive policies**.
 
 
 
• **India's Minority Upliftment Efforts:**
 
 
• Focuses on **educational, economic, and social empowerment** of minorities.
 
• Ensures inclusive growth through schemes like "**Nai Roshni**" and "**Ustaad**" aimed at skill development and heritage preservation.
 
• Contributes to reducing inequalities and fostering harmony within the country.
 
 
 
• **Global Leadership Recognition:**
 
 
• Highlights the significance of India's role in **promoting peace and development** globally.
 
• Strengthens diplomatic ties and enhances **India's global influence**.
 
• Encourages further collaboration on international platforms for addressing global challenges.

questions.question: Purple Fests (Festival of Inclusion) has been organised in India since ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purple Fests**, also known as the **Festival of Inclusion**, was first organized in **India in 2023**. The event is celebrated to promote inclusion, diversity, and equality in society.
 
• The festival focuses on creating awareness and celebrating the spirit of inclusivity, particularly emphasizing the rights and contributions of **Persons with Disabilities (PwDs)**.
 
• The inaugural Purple Fest was hosted in **Goa**, a state known for its vibrant culture and tourism, making it an ideal location to promote inclusivity.
 
• Organized by the **Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities** (Divyangjan), the Purple Fest aligns with the government's initiatives to empower marginalized communities.
 
• The event featured activities such as cultural programs, panel discussions, exhibitions, and workshops to foster understanding, collaboration, and inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purpose of Purple Fest:**

 
 
• The festival is designed to provide a platform for **Persons with Disabilities (PwDs)** to showcase their talents and engage in discussions about their rights and opportunities.
 
• It aims to bridge the gap between disabled and non-disabled communities by promoting mutual understanding and cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Key Highlights of the 2023 Purple Fest:**
 
 
• Interactive sessions on topics related to **disability rights, accessibility, and inclusion**.
 
• Exhibitions featuring assistive technologies and innovations designed to enhance the lives of PwDs.
 
• Cultural performances and showcases by artists with disabilities, emphasizing their creativity and contributions to society.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Inclusivity:**
 
 
• Inclusion ensures that every individual, regardless of their abilities, has equal opportunities to participate in all aspects of life.
 
• Events like Purple Fest play a crucial role in breaking stereotypes and fostering a more inclusive and empathetic society.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for PwDs:**
 
 
• The **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016** provides a legal framework to ensure equality and dignity for PwDs in India.
 
• Other initiatives include the **Accessible India Campaign**, which focuses on enhancing accessibility in public spaces and transportation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Venue of the First Purple Fest:** **Goa**, a state with a robust infrastructure and tourist-friendly environment, was chosen to host the inaugural event.
 
• **Global Influence:** The Purple Fest aligns with global efforts to promote inclusivity, such as the United Nations’ **Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD)**.
 
• **Annual Event:** Following its successful launch in 2023, the Purple Fest is expected to become an **annual celebration** to continue promoting inclusivity and awareness.

questions.question: _______ is a type of start which is essential for sprint races in sports.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crouch Start**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crouch Start** is a fundamental technique used in sprint races, especially in track and field events. It is designed to maximize acceleration at the beginning of the race.
 
• In the crouch start position, the sprinter's body is bent forward with knees and hands on the ground, ensuring a stable posture to push off quickly and efficiently.
 
• The crouch start consists of three primary positions: **"On your marks," "Set," and "Go."** These commands ensure readiness and proper alignment before the race begins.
 
• This type of start is essential for short-distance sprint races like the **100m, 200m, and 400m** where initial speed is crucial.
 
• The crouch start allows athletes to utilize their explosive power effectively, minimizing reaction time and maximizing propulsion during the first few meters of the race.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Standing Start:**

 
 
• Used in longer races and casual runs, the standing start involves the athlete starting from an upright position.
 
• This start is not suitable for short sprints as it reduces the efficiency of initial acceleration.
 
• It is commonly used in **middle-distance and long-distance races**.
 
 
 
• **Jumping Start:**
 
 
• The jumping start is not a recognized technique in professional sprinting.
 
• It involves launching forward without proper grounding or stability, leading to inefficiency and slower starts.
 
• This type of start may be seen in informal races or playful scenarios.
 
 
 
• **Vertical Start:**
 
 
• The vertical start involves standing upright and starting without crouching, similar to the standing start.
 
• It does not provide the explosive advantage needed for sprint races.
 
• This start is often used in **recreational or non-competitive settings**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Crouch Start:**
 
 
• The crouch start was standardized in professional sports to ensure fairness and optimal performance in sprint races.
 
• Athletes undergo rigorous training to perfect this technique, as it significantly impacts their race outcomes.
 
• Starting blocks are often used to enhance stability and provide better grip during the crouch start.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The crouch start was introduced as a standardized method in sprinting events in the late **19th century**.
 
• It has been refined over time with the introduction of starting blocks in the **1930s**.
 
• These advancements have allowed athletes to achieve faster start times and break records consistently.
 
 
 
• **Physiological Benefits:**
 
 
• The crouch start engages major muscle groups such as **quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves**, enabling explosive power.
 
• It minimizes air resistance and optimizes body posture for rapid acceleration.
 
• Proper technique is crucial to avoiding injuries and maximizing performance.

questions.question: The Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve is in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve** is located in the state of **Rajasthan**, India.
 
• It was notified as the **52nd Tiger Reserve of India** in **May 2022** under the **Project Tiger**, a conservation program initiated in 1973 to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
• The reserve is situated in the **Bundi district** of Rajasthan and serves as a critical corridor between the **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in the northeast and the **Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve** in the south.
 
• It spans an area of approximately **1,501.89 square kilometers**, which includes a **buffer zone** and a **core zone** rich in biodiversity.
 
• The reserve is home to a variety of wildlife, including **tigers, leopards, Indian wolves, striped hyenas, and sloth bears**, along with numerous species of birds and reptiles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Tiger:**

 
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched in **1973** by the **Government of India** to ensure a viable population of Bengal tigers in their natural habitats and to protect them from extinction.
 
• It is administered by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.
 
• As of **October 2023**, India has **54 tiger reserves** distributed across various states.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan and Tiger Conservation:**
 
 
• Rajasthan is home to three tiger reserves: **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve**, **Sariska Tiger Reserve**, and the newly added **Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve**.
 
• These reserves contribute significantly to the **conservation of tigers** and other wildlife species in the arid and semi-arid regions of the state.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in Ramgarh Vishdhari:**
 
 
• The reserve is characterized by its **dry deciduous forest** and rocky terrain, which provide an ideal habitat for tigers and other wildlife.
 
• It also has rich **flora and fauna**, including species like **khair, salar, dhok, and cheela**.
 
• The reserve serves as a critical **habitat corridor** for tigers migrating from neighboring reserves.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Conservation:**
 
 
• Despite efforts under Project Tiger, challenges such as **habitat fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict, and poaching** persist in tiger conservation.
 
• Effective measures, including **community participation**, **eco-development programs**, and **anti-poaching patrols**, are essential for the long-term sustainability of tiger reserves.

• The **All-India Tiger Estimation Report 2018** recorded a population of **2,967 tigers**, showcasing a significant increase in tiger numbers since 2006.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tiger Reserves:**
 
 
• Tiger reserves not only protect tigers but also serve as **conservation hubs** for other wildlife species and promote **ecotourism**.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining the **ecological balance** and supporting the livelihoods of local communities through sustainable tourism practices.
 
 
 
• **Role of NTCA:**
 
 
• The **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** was established in **2005** under the **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972** to strengthen tiger conservation initiatives.
 
• It provides **technical and financial support** to tiger reserves and oversees the implementation of policies and programs related to tiger conservation.

• Protected areas like Satkosia help in safeguarding endangered species such as the **Gharial crocodile** and preserving the natural beauty of Odisha’s landscapes.
 
• India’s growing network of protected areas underscores its commitment to global conservation goals like the **Aichi Targets** and the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the government budget?

I. Subsidies are an important policy instrument which aim at increasing welfare.

II. Defence expenditure, is committed expenditure in the sense that given the national security concerns, there exists little scope for drastic reduction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** Subsidies are an important policy instrument which aim at increasing welfare.

 
 
• Subsidies are financial assistance provided by the government to individuals, businesses, or sectors to lower the cost of goods or services and promote welfare.
 
• Subsidies are intended to address social inequalities by supporting lower-income groups and ensuring access to essential services such as health, education, and food security.
 
• Examples include subsidies for agricultural fertilizers, healthcare schemes, and education initiatives aimed at uplifting marginalized sections of society.
 
• This statement is **correct** as subsidies play a crucial role in enhancing social welfare and economic inclusivity.
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Defence expenditure is committed expenditure in the sense that given the national security concerns, there exists little scope for drastic reduction.
 
 
• Defence expenditure forms a significant part of the government budget due to national security priorities.
 
• Such spending is categorized as committed expenditure, meaning it is obligatory and cannot be drastically reduced owing to strategic and geopolitical considerations.
 
• India allocates substantial resources to defence, ranking among the top global spenders in this sector to ensure readiness against external threats and internal security challenges.
 
• This statement is **correct** as defence spending is integral to maintaining sovereignty and territorial integrity.
 
 
 
• Both statements I and II are correct, making the correct answer **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Government Budget:**

 
 
• The government budget is a financial statement outlining revenue generation and expenditure allocation for a fiscal year.
 
• It serves as a policy tool for implementing economic strategies, addressing socio-economic challenges, and promoting equitable growth.
 
• Components include capital expenditure, revenue expenditure, taxes, subsidies, and allocation for welfare programs.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies:**
 
 
• Subsidies help reduce the cost burden on essential goods and services for vulnerable sections of the population.
 
• Examples include food subsidies through the **Public Distribution System (PDS)** and educational scholarships for marginalized communities.
 
• Subsidy allocation is determined based on socio-economic priorities and is subject to annual revisions.
 
 
 
• **Defence Expenditure:**
 
 
• India's defence budget for **2023-24** was approximately **₹5.93 lakh crore**, highlighting its importance in national security.
 
• Spending covers areas such as personnel salaries, equipment procurement, infrastructure development, and research.
 
• India is among the top global spenders on defence, given its strategic location and geopolitical challenges.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Budget Allocation:**
 
 
• It ensures the effective utilization of resources to achieve developmental goals and maintain economic stability.
 
• Allocation priorities reflect government policies, addressing areas like poverty alleviation, healthcare, education, and infrastructure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Subsidy Management:**

 
 
• Subsidies should be implemented efficiently to prevent misuse and ensure targeted benefits for the intended beneficiaries.
 
• Periodic audits and monitoring mechanisms are essential to maintain transparency in subsidy distribution.
 
 
 
• **Defence Spending Trends:**
 
 
• India's defence spending has been steadily rising due to advancements in technology and increasing security concerns.
 
• Collaborations with international defence organizations and private companies enhance capabilities and reduce dependence on imports.
 
 
 
• **Budget Reforms:**
 
 
• Reforms like digitization of transactions and direct benefit transfers (DBT) have improved the efficiency of subsidy and budget implementation.
 
• Innovative approaches, such as outcome-based budgeting, ensure greater accountability and effective resource utilization.

questions.question:
Which of the following qualifications is required to contest the election of the President of India?

I. He or she must hold any office of profit under Central government.

II. He or she must qualify to become member of House of the People.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eligibility to Contest for the President of India:**

 
 
• As per **Article 58** of the **Constitution of India**, the individual must be a citizen of India.
 
• The individual must have completed the age of **35 years**.
 
• The candidate must be qualified for election as a member of the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha). ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Office of Profit:**
 
 
• To contest the election for the President of India, the individual must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India, any state government, or any local authority.
 
• Holding an office of profit disqualifies a candidate from contesting the Presidential election as per constitutional provisions. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• The President of India is elected by an electoral college composed of elected members of both houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The election is conducted using a system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 58 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 58 lays down the eligibility criteria to contest the election for the President of India.
 
• The candidate must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India, state government, or any subordinate authority.
 
• He/she must fulfill qualifications for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, which includes **citizenship of India**, minimum age of **25 years**, and adherence to other disqualification clauses.
 
 
 
• **Election Process of President:**
 
 
• The election is conducted by the **Election Commission of India**.
 
• It involves an **electoral college** comprising elected representatives from Parliament and Legislative Assemblies.
 
• The election follows the **single transferable vote system** to ensure proportional representation.
 
 
 
• **Office of Profit:**
 
 
• The term "office of profit" refers to a position that brings financial gain or remuneration to the holder.
 
• It is a disqualification criterion for contesting certain elections, including that of the President, as per constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Important Presidential Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• He/she must not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature.
 
• He/she must not have any financial interest in government contracts or works.
 
• He/she must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or state governments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electoral College:**

 
 
• Includes elected members of the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
 
• Nominated members are excluded from the electoral process.
 
• Votes are weighted based on the population of the states represented.
 
 
 
• **Single Transferable Vote System:**
 
 
• Allows voters to rank candidates in order of preference.
 
• Ensures proportional representation in the election of the President.
 
• Votes are transferred to the next preference if the first preference candidate is eliminated.
 
 
 
• **Role of Election Commission:**
 
 
• Conducts and supervises the Presidential election process.
 
• Ensures transparency and adherence to constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Disqualification Criteria:**
 
 
• Holding an office of profit under the government.
 
• Being an undischarged insolvent.
 
• Non-compliance with eligibility criteria mentioned under Article 58.

questions.question: Rajya Sabha is required to return a Money Bill passed and transmitted by Lok Sabha within a period of _______ days from the date of its receipt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** has limited powers concerning a Money Bill under the **Indian Constitution**. It cannot reject or amend a Money Bill and must return it to the Lok Sabha within a stipulated time.
 
• As per **Article 110** of the **Indian Constitution**, if a Money Bill is passed by the Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, the latter must return it within **14 days** from the date of its receipt.
 
• If the **Rajya Sabha** fails to return the Money Bill within this period, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The 14-day time limit is crucial to ensure that financial legislation is not unduly delayed, as the Union Government relies on such bills for its fiscal management.
 
• This limitation on Rajya Sabha’s powers ensures the supremacy of the **Lok Sabha** in financial matters, as Lok Sabha directly represents the people through elected members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of a Money Bill:**

 
 
• As per **Article 110**, a Money Bill deals exclusively with matters like the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes, the borrowing of money by the government, or the appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and their decision is final.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• In financial matters, the **Lok Sabha** has overriding powers due to its direct accountability to the electorate.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** can discuss a Money Bill and suggest amendments, but it cannot reject or amend it without the consent of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Process of Passing a Money Bill:**
 
 
• A Money Bill is introduced only in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• After the Lok Sabha passes it, the bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for consideration.
 
• The Rajya Sabha must return the bill within **14 days**, either with recommendations or without, after which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject the recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 14-Day Rule:**
 
 
• The time limit ensures that financial legislation is passed promptly, avoiding delays in government functioning.
 
• This rule upholds the principle of **parliamentary accountability**, as the Lok Sabha, being a directly elected body, has the final say in matters concerning public finance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Ordinary Bills:**
 
 
• For ordinary bills, the Rajya Sabha has equal legislative powers with the Lok Sabha and can suggest amendments, reject, or hold a bill for six months.
 
• However, for Money Bills, its powers are restricted as per the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the other name of the tissue fluid in human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lymph**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lymph** is the other name for tissue fluid, which is a clear fluid that circulates throughout the lymphatic system in the human body.
 
• Tissue fluid is formed when blood plasma leaks out of capillaries into surrounding tissues, facilitating the exchange of nutrients, oxygen, and waste products between blood and cells.
 
• Lymph is similar to blood plasma but lacks red blood cells and large proteins, making it a lighter fluid.
 
• The primary function of lymph is to collect and return interstitial fluid back to the bloodstream, thus maintaining fluid balance in the body.
 
• Lymph also plays a vital role in the immune system by transporting white blood cells (lymphocytes) and filtering harmful substances through lymph nodes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lymphatic System:**

 
 
• The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, nodes, and organs that work together to transport lymph throughout the body.
 
• It consists of lymphatic vessels, lymph nodes, the spleen, thymus, and tonsils.
 
• Lymph nodes act as filters, trapping pathogens and foreign particles to prevent them from entering the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Tissue Fluid:**
 
 
• Tissue fluid is formed through the process of filtration at the capillary level, where hydrostatic pressure forces plasma out of blood vessels.
 
• Approximately 90% of this fluid is reabsorbed into the capillaries, while the remaining 10% enters the lymphatic system as lymph.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Lymph:**
 
 
• Maintains fluid balance by collecting excess interstitial fluid and returning it to the blood circulation.
 
• Facilitates the removal of waste products and toxins from tissues.
 
• Supports immunity by transporting lymphocytes and antibodies to sites of infection.
 
• Aids in the absorption of fats and fat-soluble vitamins from the digestive system through lacteals in the small intestine.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Sweat:** Sweat is produced by sweat glands and primarily aids in temperature regulation and excretion of salts. It is not tissue fluid.
 
• **Urine:** Urine is excreted by the kidneys to remove waste and excess water from the body. It is unrelated to tissue fluid.
 
• **Mucus:** Mucus is produced by mucous membranes to protect and lubricate surfaces, such as the respiratory and digestive tracts, and is different from lymph.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lymph Nodes:**

 
 
• Lymph nodes are small bean-shaped structures located along lymphatic vessels.
 
• They contain immune cells such as lymphocytes and macrophages that attack and destroy pathogens.
 
• Swelling in lymph nodes may indicate an infection or disease, such as cancer.
 
 
 
• **Pathway of Lymph:**
 
 
• Lymph flows from lymphatic capillaries to larger lymphatic vessels and eventually drains into the bloodstream via the thoracic duct or right lymphatic duct.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Importance:**
 
 
• Disorders of the lymphatic system include lymphedema, lymphoma, and infections such as tonsillitis.
 
• Maintaining a healthy lymphatic system is crucial for immunity and fluid balance in the body.

questions.question: Who was the Pallava king that built the 'seven rathas' at Mahabalipuram?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narasimhavarman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narasimhavarman I**, also known as **Mamalla**, was one of the most significant rulers of the Pallava dynasty in South India.
 
• He ruled from **630 CE to 668 CE** and was known for his architectural contributions and military conquests.
 
• The **'Seven Rathas'** or the **Panch Rathas** at Mahabalipuram were built during his reign. These are rock-cut monolithic temples designed in the shape of chariots.
 
• The monuments at Mahabalipuram were created to showcase the Pallava dynasty's artistic and architectural brilliance and are now recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• Narasimhavarman is also remembered for defeating the Chalukya king **Pulakesin II** and taking control of the Chalukyan capital of Vatapi, earning him the title **Vatapikonda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahabalipuram:**

 
 
• Located on the Coromandel Coast, Mahabalipuram is famous for its **rock-cut architecture** and **monolithic temples**.
 
• The site includes the **Shore Temple**, cave temples, and the **Panch Rathas**, which are an excellent example of Pallava architecture.
 
• Mahabalipuram served as a major port city during the Pallava dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India from the **3rd century CE to the 9th century CE**.
 
• They were known for their contributions to **art, architecture**, and the spread of **Brahmanical and Dravidian culture**.
 
• Their capital was at **Kanchipuram**, which was an important center of learning and religion.
 
 
 
• **Seven Rathas:**
 
 
• The 'Seven Rathas' or Panch Rathas are named after the Pandavas and Draupadi from the Mahabharata.
 
• They are carved out of **single granite blocks** and exhibit different architectural styles.
 
• Each ratha is dedicated to a deity and is a prototype of various temple styles.
 
 
 
• **Narasimhavarman's Military Achievements:**
 
 
• He defeated the Chalukya king Pulakesin II in the **Battle of Vatapi** around 642 CE, a significant victory in South Indian history.
 
• He extended the Pallava influence over much of South India during his reign.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Significance:** The monuments at Mahabalipuram mark the transition from rock-cut to structural temples in South Indian architecture.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** The group of monuments at Mahabalipuram was designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1984**.
 
• **Vatapikonda Title:** The title "Vatapikonda" (Conqueror of Vatapi) reflects Narasimhavarman's military prowess and successful campaigns.
 
• **Legacy:** Narasimhavarman's reign is remembered as a golden age of **Pallava art and culture**, leaving a lasting impact on South Indian history and architecture.
